why: Settled (Readings, half b): a self-reference looks back at the fixed-up path only; the original-path fallback is for the application root (L1043-1047), which a field referring to itself does not — unlike 009/011/014, where an optional vanishes without a cycle and the root must still be tried. A self-reference looks back at the field's own earlier value (L747-749), here at its fixed-up path; the fallback to the original path is for an included file that "might intend to refer to the application's root config" (L1043-1047), which a field referring to itself does not. typesafe/config reads it so: a += 2 included at k is k.a = ${?k.a} [2], k.a has no earlier value, and the root's unrelated a = [1] is not looked at: k.a is [2]. lightbend/config#863 retries the including root when an included optional vanishes without a cycle, and keeps a swallowed cycle from falling back, so this row stays as it is.
